dedupe_keys.name: emergency warning dissemination in a multiplex social network agent based monte carlo model coos bay and seaside oregon

description: This agent-based model estimates how an emergency warning spreads through a threatened community when official broadcast is combined with people warning each other. The CoMSES Net release read on 2026-09-28 (version 1.0.0, published 31 January 2023 by Charles Koll) models a multiplex social network of three informal channels, phone, word of mouth and social media, each with its own attributes; once warned, each individual may warn others with a probability that depends on how they were warned and the time left until impact. Monte Carlo runs compare the relative effects of broadcast and contagion. Default parameters come from empirical studies of disaster warnings and the spatial layout of Coos Bay and Seaside, two Oregon coastal towns exposed to Cascadia tsunamis. It is written in Julia. Access is free download under the MIT licence. Caveats: the network structure is synthetic and the model is not calibrated to a real event. It supports emergency response studies, such as testing whether siren or cell broadcast coverage gaps can be closed by social warning before a tsunami arrives. No related warning dissemination model is catalogued.
inputs: warning channel attributes (phone, word of mouth, social media)
name: Emergency warning dissemination in a multiplex social network: agent-based Monte Carlo model (Coos Bay and Seaside, Oregon)
outputs: share of population warned over time
relative effect of broadcast and contagion
